90701.text: How many parts does the Operations Manual consist of, and what are they?
options: Four: General/Basic, Aircraft Operating, Route and Aerodrome, Training
Five: General, Aircraft, Route, Training, Safety

90702.text: In which part of the Operations Manual are the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) and the Configuration Deviation List (CDL) found?
options: Part A – General and Basic Information
Part C – Route and Aerodrome Instructions
In a separate appendix, not in any part

90703.text: Aerodrome operating minima and the instructions for their calculation are found in which part of the Operations Manual?
options: Part C – Route and Aerodrome Instructions and Information
Part A – General and Basic Information

90704.text: Following a medical procedure requiring local anaesthesia, how much time must elapse at minimum before a flight crew member may report for duty?

90705.text: What is the prescribed period for a flight crew member following a medical procedure requiring general anaesthesia?

90706.text: After donating blood, how much time must elapse at minimum before a flight crew member may commence duty?

90707.text: A flight crew member must not consume alcohol starting how many hours before commencing duty or standby?

90708.text: What is the blood alcohol level limit above which a flight crew member may not commence duty?

90709.text: Integrating a flight data analysis programme into the safety management system is mandatory for organisations operating which aircraft?
options: Aircraft with a maximum take-off mass exceeding 27,000 kilograms
Aircraft with a maximum take-off mass exceeding 5,700 kilograms
Aircraft with a maximum take-off mass exceeding 136,000 kilograms

90710.text: At the authority's request, within what maximum period must the operator provide all documents and records?

90711.text: Under certification requirements, within what maximum time must an aircraft be capable of being evacuated with a full passenger load?

90712.text: Which of the following is correct regarding the flight recorder?
options: It records the last 25 hours and recordings are retained for at least 60 days
It records the last 2 hours and recordings are retained for at least 30 days
It records the last 25 hours and recordings are retained for at least 6 months
It records the last 10 hours and recordings are retained for at least 60 days
There is no recording time limit; recordings are retained indefinitely

90713.text: On which frequency does an Emergency Locator Transmitter (ELT) transmit its signal?

90714.text: What does a "MINIMUM FUEL" declaration mean?
options: The usable fuel remaining has reached a level that leaves no allowance for unexpected delays; it is not an emergency
The aircraft has descended below final reserve fuel and an emergency landing is required
Absolute landing priority is being requested from ATC
The destination cannot be reached without refuelling

90715.text: What does a "MAYDAY FUEL" call indicate?
options: It is certain that landing will occur with less than final reserve fuel remaining; it is an emergency
Fuel leaves no allowance for unexpected delays
A decision has been made to divert to an alternate aerodrome

90716.text: How many sensitive pressure altimeters are required under the minimum equipment requirements for IFR flight?

90717.text: In addition to IFR equipment, how many landing lights are mandatory for night flight?
options: A landing light is not mandatory

90718.text: How is alternate aerodrome fuel calculated for propeller-driven aircraft?
options: Fuel to fly to the most critical alternate plus 45 minutes; or 15% of the planned flight time at cruising levels plus an additional 45 minutes
Fuel to fly to the most critical alternate plus 30 minutes
10% of cruise time plus an additional 30 minutes
Fuel to fly to the alternate plus a 30-minute hold at 1,500 ft
Half the flight time to the destination aerodrome

90719.text: For turbo-jet powered aircraft, under what conditions is holding over the alternate aerodrome assumed when calculating alternate fuel?
options: At standard temperature, 30 minutes at 1,500 ft AGL above the alternate
At standard temperature, 45 minutes at 1,000 ft AGL above the alternate
30 minutes at 3,000 ft AGL above the alternate
45 minutes at 1,500 ft AGL above the alternate

90720.text: Which of the following is not required for refuelling to be carried out while passengers are on board?
options: All aircraft doors being open and the stairs connected
Qualified personnel being available to initiate and direct an evacuation
Two-way communication being established between the refuelling supervisor and the ground crew
At least one suitable door being ready for evacuation with its paths unobstructed

90721.text: During ditching, when wave height is significant, how should the landing be made?
options: Parallel to the swell direction and onto the back of the wave
Perpendicular to the wave and onto the crest of the wave
Always into wind regardless of conditions
Parallel to the swell direction and onto the front of the wave
At the highest possible speed, perpendicular to the wave

90722.text: In which configuration should the aircraft be put down on the water during ditching?
options: Landing gear up, wings level, nose slightly up, and at minimum safe speed
Landing gear down, wings level, nose down
Landing gear up, the aircraft stalled onto the water
Landing gear down, at maximum speed
Wings banked, nose down, landing gear up

90723.text: Which of the following is correct regarding Runway Status Lights (RWSL)?
options: They only indicate the status of the runway; they do not constitute clearance for take-off or runway entry
When illuminated green, they indicate that the runway may be entered
They are the visual equivalent of a take-off clearance issued by the tower
They operate only in low-visibility conditions
They are used to provide taxi guidance

90724.text: The enhanced taxiway centreline marking extends back approximately how many metres from the runway-holding position?

90725.text: If a carburettor fire occurs during engine start and the engine has not started, what should be done?
options: Select mixture to Idle Cut-Off, open the throttle fully, and continue cranking to draw the flame into the engine
Enrich the mixture and stop cranking immediately
Run the engine at high power for a while
Leave the fuel on and fight the fire with an extinguisher
Leave the master switch on and inform the tower

90726.text: Which of the following is the type of fire extinguisher required to be carried in the cockpit?
options: Dry powder for metal fires only
There is no requirement to carry an extinguisher

90727.text: What is the typical diameter of a microburst?

90728.text: Approximately how long does a microburst last?

90729.text: In large aircraft, what is the maximum airspeed that can occur within the core of a wake vortex?

90730.text: For noise abatement purposes, pilots should not turn during take-off and climb until reaching which altitude?

90731.text: What is the maximum bank angle permitted for turns made on noise-preferential routes?

90732.text: Which of the following is correct regarding the selection of a take-off alternate?
options: There is no distance or time requirement, such as 1 hour or 2 hours, depending on the number of engines
For single-engine aircraft, it must be within 1 hour at most
For multi-engine aircraft, it must be within 2 hours at most
It must be within 100 NM of the departure aerodrome at most
It must always be the same as the destination alternate

90733.text: What is the maximum take-off mass threshold for the definition of a "large aircraft"?

90734.text: Which are the critical phases of flight during which portable electronic devices (PEDs) must be secured?

90735.text: How many parts does ICAO Annex 6 (Operation of Aircraft) consist of?
options: Three: International Commercial Air Transport – Aeroplanes, International General Aviation – Aeroplanes, International Operations – Helicopters
Four: Commercial, General, Helicopter and UAV
Five: Commercial, General, Helicopter, Balloon and Glider
